authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth; _repo_validation_matrix.json is generated from it.

common_sense_validation_policy.validate_lane: Validators inspect and report release-threatening integrity risk only. They do not build, publish, promote, absorb, apply, deploy, bootstrap runtimes, or mutate providers.
common_sense_validation_policy.execute_lane: Build, generate, normalize, repair, absorb, apply, publish, distribute, and self-heal commands must live in explicit build, execute, release, workflow, citation, apply, or repair lanes.

hard_fail_bases.repo_integrity: secrets, package integrity, wrong repo root, conflict markers, corrupted or overwritten canonical source, protected raw agent artifacts mutated
hard_fail_bases.build_integrity: the site or a workflow cannot build or run: broken build cache, workflow YAML that cannot parse, a workflow command pointing at nothing
hard_fail_bases.public_route_integrity: a served URL is broken, duplicated, quarantined or routed to the wrong vertical/domain; broken internal links or assets
hard_fail_bases.aeo_seo_geo_vital: an indexable page is missing a search/answer-engine vital: title, meta description, canonical, exactly one h1, readable encoding, crawler access, sitemap parity, truthful schema
hard_fail_bases.user_safety_or_false_public_claim: regulated advice crossing a boundary, a public claim without evidence, or internal build text shown to readers
hard_fail_bases.foreign_input: an arriving agent drop is malformed (unparseable, missing or typoed artifacts). A well-formed drop that is merely not yet worked is never a failure
hard_fail_bases.published_content_loss: content already delivered to readers, or paid measurements, silently destroyed

common_sense_validation_policy.enforced_by: scripts/validation/validate_validation_registry.js: every ACTIVE HARD_FAIL validator must declare hard_fail_basis from hard_fail_bases, and no more than MAX_HARD_FAIL may exist

HARD_FAIL.meaning: Direct production, user-safety, evidence, route, workflow, build, or delivery threat; never cosmetic formatting.

STRONG_WARNING.meaning: Material quality, ingestion, indexing, accessibility, or performance degradation.

SOFT_WARNING.meaning: Maintainability, documentation, style, or low-risk quality concern.

INFO.meaning: Metric, observation, historical evidence, or optimization note.

scope_definitions.CONTAINER: Runnable in the standard container without provider credentials.
scope_definitions.LOCAL_ONLY: Requires deployed URL, browser runtime, credentials, or operator environment.

core.description: Pure default release-blocking checks; no mutation and no external provider dependency.

release.description: Full container release proof: core plus source immutability, hygiene, and deterministic build.

strict.description: Release proof plus advisory checks; warnings remain visible but do not block.

advisory.description: Non-blocking quality and ingestion warnings only.

local.description: Full release proof plus deployed Playwright click audit.

audit.description: Collect-all execution of every active and on-demand validator; local-only checks are deferred unless explicitly enabled.

social.description: Public-signal normalization and candidate loop validation.

llm.description: LLM export, answer-block, entity-graph, and citation-target validation.

homepages.description: Homepage-only schema and assistance boundary checks.

canonical-data.description: Protected canonical source static and runtime immutability checks.

postrelease.description: Pure post-build structural verification; no content release or mutation.

content-release.description: Lean content-release checks for generated static content and routing contracts.

agent-run.description: Agent artifact ingestion, FIX compilation, exact implementation, and semantic acceptance proof.

full-audit.description: Hostile collect-all review of all active validators without pretending every advisory check belongs in core.

citation-intelligence.description: Traffic-qualified citation intelligence, proof packet, atom, structural graph, and workflow topology gates.

deep-isolated.description: Isolated deep container validation: workflow data trace, browserless mock backup, and traffic-qualified citation intelligence only. No real browser claim.

validators.title: Canonical-domain contract and brand separation

Since 16 Oct 2026 it also fails if any canonical-domain href on an insights page is not in that canonical site's sitemap route list (data/canonical_route_snapshot.json, refreshed by scripts/refresh_canonical_route_snapshot.js), or if zero such links were checked. It also fails if any theindustryguides.com href on an insights page does not resolve to an ADMITTED (published) route, a static file or a _redirects source, or if zero internal links were checked. It also fails if any page URL in sitemap.xml or sitemaps/*.xml has no internal inbound link from another served page, if the homepage stops linking /insights/ and /atlas/, or if zero sitemap URLs were checked. Since 12 Oct 2026 it also fails if any built file in dist/ or any Pages Function source names Spry Labs, spryvc.com, joinwestpeek.com or westpeek.ventures, or if functions/api/request-assistance.js stops pinning the lead sender to The Industry Guides <hello@theindustryguides.com> (or reads env.EMAIL_FROM). Until then every lead email from theindustryguides.com went out From hello@joinwestpeek.com, hardcoded in wrangler.toml. Zero dist or function files scanned is a failure. wrangler.toml is out of scope by design: it carries the recipient (LEAD_TO), which no visitor sees.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: Render checks do not prove the approved canonical domain mapping. Nothing else read the Pages Function source or scanned every dist file for another company's name or domain.
validators.unit_attribution_measured: 12 Oct 2026: appending hello@joinwestpeek.com to dist/about.html failed the validator (exit 1); scripts/tests/test_brand_separation.js constructs each failing state (function sender, dist name, env.EMAIL_FROM read, missing pin, zero dist files, zero function files). 12 Oct 2026 (weekly report): setting FROM = "os@westpeek.ventures" in scripts/search_console/search_outcomes_weekly.py failed the validator (exit 1, two failures: forbidden sender domain + unpinned sender); restored, exit 0. Sending code (scripts/ and functions/ files calling api.resend.com) and every workflow now scanned; zero of either fails.

validators.title: Build-result cache is byte-identical to a real build
validators.risk_prevented: A stale or corrupted cache entry restoring the wrong bytes onto a `npm run build:cached` no-op run - the entire 2,070-page site regenerated from scratch on every CI invocation was this repo's actual cost before this cache existed, and a cache that is fast but wrong is worse than no cache at all. This validator requires a cache entry for the CURRENT input hash, rejects one that never came from a completed build (readEntryMeta refuses a missing/false build_completed stamp or a mismatched input_hash before any file is touched), and then hashes every git-tracked file plus the cache-managed build dirs on both the current tree and an isolated, cache-disabled ground-truth rebuild - not a sample - and fails naming the exact files that differ.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: deterministic-build proves two independent builds of the same source agree with each other. It says nothing about the cache: a cache entry could be stale, partially written, or restored against the wrong input hash and deterministic-build would never see it, because it never runs `npm run build:cached` or inspects .build-cache/ at all. It is audit-only and not on the merge gate, deliberately: the gate runs four stages after site-build that write into data/, which is part of the cache's hashed input surface, so by validation time the hash has moved and this validator looks for an entry no build ever used. The gate's guard over the same mechanism is the wrapper itself: scripts/build_cache_wrapper.js refuses to exit 0 on an entry it cannot read back complete, or with the store inside the repo tree under CI, and the lane runs it as its site-build stage - which generated-content-finalization-contract pins. That needs no blocker of its own.

validators.title: Primary-source and claim registry integrity, including retired authority URLs
validators.risk_prevented: Regulated or numeric pages could ship with missing, dangling, or malformed provenance records. ALSO PINS RETIRED AUTHORITY URLS (16 Oct 2026). Every state page cites a licensing board or a federal programme page by URL, and those publishers move pages without redirecting. Danielle's site-audit crawl of theindustryguides.com found nine such links serving 404 from live guide pages: the Montana, Iowa, South Dakota, Connecticut and Tennessee psychology boards, the Tennessee medical board, the CMS state-based exchange list, and the Georgia Medicaid dental fee schedule, whose quarterly PDF filename carries a publication timestamp GAMMIS rotates so a direct link rots within three months. A claim sourced to a dead URL is the root of a false public claim, which is this validator's own hard_fail_basis, so the pin lives here rather than as a forty-first blocker. scripts/lib/retired_authority_urls.js holds the retired/live pairs and the evidence for each; this validator calls it. It fails when a retired URL reappears in the evidence or page-family source files or in any rendered HTML, AND when a replacement URL is absent from the source files, which is what 'fixed to nothing' looks like. Deliberately offline: a live crawl in CI would go red on a publisher bot-blocking us (ftc.gov 404s its own root to this egress) or on a hosting outage (medicaid.ms.gov was serving a temporary-site notice on 2026-10-16); both were investigated on 16 Oct and left unpinned because neither was a defect on our side.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: The content-atom gate proves structure and uniqueness, not source identity, claim linkage, retrieval dates, or recheck governance. For the retired-URL pin: the https/dated/claim-class checks above cannot know whether a URL resolves, rendered-internal-hrefs checks internal hrefs only, and nothing in the repository looked at outbound authority links at all - which is why nine of them 404'd for months. The pin self-tests four cases on synthetic text every run, including an empty corpus that must fail rather than pass vacuously.
validators.failure_action: for a retired-URL failure: re-check the publisher's current URL with a browser user agent AND its host root (a 403 or 404 on the root means the publisher is blocking us, not that the page died), repair data/evidence/* and data/page_families/velocity_page_specs.json, rebuild, and update the pair in scripts/lib/retired_authority_urls.js; stop release and repair

validators.title: MedicalWebPage and PriceSpecification are emitted and match the page
validators.risk_prevented: Prevents the medical schema types the citation runs asked for from being declared but not emitted, and prevents price markup quoting a figure the reader cannot see. content/_live/pages.json carried a schema_eligibility.medical_web_page flag on 220 records that no code path read.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: The existing schema checks assert Article, FAQPage, HowTo and BreadcrumbList. None asserts the medical types, and none checks that a price in the markup is also visible on the page.
validators.unit_attribution_measured: Every one of the six arrays was measured against a constructed failing state on 2026-09-09, not inferred from the source. Rewriting "MedicalWebPage" to "WebPage" in trt/index.html produced missing_medical_web_page: ["trt/index.html"]; adding a MedicalWebPage node to personal-injury/index.html produced medical_web_page_on_non_medical_route: ["personal-injury/index.html"]; rewriting "PriceSpecification" in dentistry/dental-implants/index.html produced missing_price_specification: ["dentistry/dental-implants/index.html"]; shifting a minPrice in dentistry/clear-aligners/index.html produced price_mismatch: [{file: "dentistry/clear-aligners/index.html", ...}]; changing the visible "$3,000" on that same page produced price_in_markup_not_visible_on_page: [{file: ...}]; corrupting a JSON-LD block produced json_ld_parse_failures: [{file: ...}]. Three arrays hold bare path strings and three hold objects keyed by file, which is why each is declared separately rather than assumed. Every row names the rendered file the validator itself read, so the failure belongs to that page's unit and to no other.

validators.title: Lead submissions from BLOCKED_LEAD_DOMAINS are dropped quietly; all others are stored
validators.risk_prevented: 26 Oct 2026 owner ruling: guide-site form submissions from blocked email domains (the BLOCKED_LEAD_DOMAINS Pages env var, comma-separated, never written in this repo) are dropped quietly - no Airtable write, no relay email, the honeypot's bare { ok: true }, one BLOCKED_LEAD log line. Fails when a blocked exact domain or subdomain reaches Airtable or Resend, when the response or log differs, or when an unlisted, look-alike or unset-env submission is not stored and relayed (a real lead silently lost).
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: No other validator executes functions/api/request-assistance.js; brand-separation only scans its text. This runs onRequestPost with a stubbed fetch over 10 cases on fake .test domains.
validators.failure_action: fix blockedLeadDomain / the block check in functions/api/request-assistance.js and re-run
validators.severity_note: STRONG_WARNING, not HARD_FAIL: the HARD_FAIL cap (40) is full, and a blocked sender getting through is a nuisance, not a release-blocking harm.

validators.title: Published pages contain no internal build instructions
validators.risk_prevented: Agent recommendations are internal build directives shaped like 'FILEPATH: x || CURRENT: ... || EDIT: ...'. Two generator paths rendered them as reader-facing copy - a fallback acceptance-checklist card, and target.answer via 'Citation-ready update: '. 163 published pages carried the first and 100 the second, the latter inside the direct-answer block that answer engines extract. It also caused the external agent to re-flag pages marked released, because it was reading its own instruction back off the page.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: Substance and extraction validators measure whether required blocks exist; none asserted that page copy is free of build directives, so filler containing the instruction counted as content.
validators.failure_action: stop the generator emitting recommendation text (scripts/lib/agent_exact_repairs.js); a fallback card announcing a content gap must not publish
validators._retired_prepare_reason: Unreachable: every prerequisite is a committed file, so run_validation_registry.js could never fire this prepare. These validators grade the committed rendered tree, which is the tree that was pushed; the declared refresh never ran and claiming it did was the untruth.
validators.unit_attribution_measured: Measured on 2026-09-09 against a constructed failing state: appending "FILEPATH: trt/index.html || EDIT: add a table" to trt/index.html produced offenders: [{path: "trt/index.html", reason: "raw agent recommendation (FILEPATH:)", shapes: ["filepath", "field-separator"]}] and exit 1. offenders is an OFFENDERS-ONLY array - a page sealed in data/content/internal_instruction_leak_baseline.json goes to `sealed` and never to `offenders` - so a row here is always a page that failed, never a page that was merely examined. The leaked instruction text is authored onto the page by the generator pass for that page, so the page is the correct charge. This validator walks the whole tree rather than this release's scope, so a leak on an untouched page resolves to a route outside the mutation scope and stays systemic, exactly as with rendered-output-shrink-guard.

validators.title: Occupancy measurement file may not shrink
validators.risk_prevented: Detects destruction of paid citation-occupancy measurements. On 2026-08-29 a scheduled run rewrote data/signals/query_class_occupancy.json without --merge and 205 recorded readings became 36: 170 grounded provider calls deleted by a run that exited 0 and reported success. The missing --merge was fixed the same day and the file was NOT rehydrated, because nothing in the repo knew how many readings there were supposed to be. This holds the expected depth outside the file, ratchets it upward only, and hard-fails when the measurement file falls below it or when a query that once carried a reading no longer does. A query may leave the panel only via an explicit retired_queries entry carrying a reason. Hard-fails on zero probes examined and on an empty high-water mark.
validators.failure_action: restore the truncated readings from a prior commit and re-derive with --rescore-only; never advance the mark to match the damage
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: occupancy-probe-contract and occupancy-control-separation both validate the CONTENTS of whatever rows the file happens to hold; both passed at 36 rows and would pass at 1. Neither knows how many rows there ought to be, so neither can see the file being truncated.

validators.title: No page loses content without a named reason
validators.risk_prevented: Prevents a thaw-rebuild-reaccept cycle installing a thinner page as the new baseline. That is exactly how 14 KB and 22 KB of delivered content left two dentistry pages with CI green. Floors rise only; a page below its floor fails unless data/release/rendered_size_baseline.json names the shrink and the byte count it may fall to - a lowered floor, so a page that later grows above that size passes (2026-09-26, Validate Repo run 36225602982 went red on a page that had GAINED 634 bytes over its licence) and a page below it fails. A floor seeded today cannot see a page that was ALREADY re-frozen thinner - a sibling repo audited on the same day had 18 in that state - so data/release/historic_page_maximum.json enumerates this repo's 862 routes below their historic maximum (111 of which lost 626 delivered artifact blocks) as a shrink-only ratchet, and a new occurrence fails.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: published-inventory-stability counts pages and frozen-output-integrity hashes accepted bytes. Neither notices a page that is still present, still frozen and still hashing correctly after being re-accepted several kilobytes smaller.
validators.repair_scope: NO REPAIR, AND NONE IS POSSIBLE BY COMMAND. This failure names a rendered page that came back from a build smaller than its accepted floor. Clearing it requires a judgment only a person can make: either the lost bytes are real content and must be RESTORED, or the shrink is correct - a duplicate cut, scaffolding deleted, content deliberately removed - and belongs in justified_shrinks in data/release/rendered_size_baseline.json WITH A WRITTEN REASON, which is the guard's own designed acceptance path and not a lowering of the bar. The previous registration claimed "npm run measure:historic-page-maximum", which writes data/release/historic_page_maximum.json; the failing verdict, unjustified_shrinks, is computed from data/release/rendered_size_baseline.json, which that command never touches. It ran against a live failure in Velocity Content Release run 34416882965, exited 0, changed nothing, and stranded the publish. With no repair declared, the guard stays HARD_FAIL in validate:release and blocks merges to main; what it no longer does is strand a publish it cannot unblock.

validators.title: The served tree keeps the head and disclosure contract: title 30-65, description 120-160 (fails only below 75% of a floor; over a ceiling never fails, the installer trims), complete social set, Organization with logo, ownership disclosure, capped link concentration
validators.risk_prevented: Search Readiness audit of theindustryguides.com, 2026-10-25, measured in dist/: 414 titles over 65 characters, 1,327 meta descriptions over 160, 1,261 pages with no og:title, 1,262 without twitter:card summary_large_image, 2,137 with no common-ownership line and 2,137 with no Organization logo, plus one insight page linking a single canonical URL eight times (8 of 11 outbound links). 2,116 of the 2,136 admitted routes are frozen accepted bytes, so a generator-only fix cannot reach them; scripts/install_served_head_contract.js fixes them at publish time and this validator holds the result. It shares scripts/lib/served_head_contract.js with the installer, so the rule has one definition, and it refuses to pass having graded fewer than 1,500 pages.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: search-snippet-floors reads the frozen repo-root pages and only enforces floors, so it cannot see a ceiling breach or anything the publish-time passes add; no validator read dist/ - the bytes the edge actually serves - for social tags, the Organization logo, the ownership disclosure or outbound-link concentration.
validators.failure_action: record finding and continue. Fix at the source: the bands live in scripts/lib/search_snippet.js, the transforms in scripts/lib/served_head_contract.js, and the generators are scripts/build_site.js (renderLayout, templates/layout.html) and scripts/lib/publish_contract.js. Never edit a rendered page.

validators.title: No tracked file carries a git conflict marker
validators.risk_prevented: A tracked file could reach main carrying git conflict markers. On 2026-09-09 PRs #99, #100 and #101 were each rebased onto a main that had moved and the conflicts - all in regenerable validation receipts - were resolved with directory pathspecs (git checkout --theirs -- artifacts), which silently leaves any file git had already written markers into exactly as it found it. 28 receipts reached main corrupted, 828 marker lines in validation-summary-release.json alone. Nothing caught it: JSON with a conflict marker does not parse, so every reader fell into a catch and treated the file as ABSENT rather than corrupt - publish_gate_decision.mjs could not read the release summary at all. A corrupt receipt is worse than a missing one because it looks present. This scans every tracked text file for a marker at the start of a line.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: repo-hygiene checks packaging and file placement, not file contents. Every validator that reads a JSON receipt wraps the parse in a try/catch and falls back to a default, which is what made this invisible rather than loud. No check anywhere read a tracked file looking for corruption, so a conflict marker could be committed, merged and carried indefinitely.
validators.failure_action: stop release and widen the lane commit surface, or stop the lane committing a state it did not validate

validators.title: A fix recorded as released is shown by its page
validators.risk_prevented: finalize_content_release.js marked a recommendation RELEASED_VERIFIED whenever its ROUTE completed a freeze transaction, which says nothing about whether the requested edit reached the page. On 2026-09-02 all 51 rows of a TRT run were marked released because trt/index.html was thawed for an unrelated spec; 12 of their required_markers were absent and stayed absent. That mark is terminal - prepare_velocity_intake_release.js excludes released ids from selection forever - so the work was recorded as delivered and retired unworked. Across the whole ledger 668 of 2,558 released claims were not shown by their pages. This fails if any fix claiming a released status is missing a required_marker from its rendered file.
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: agent-run-absorption-completeness joins a run's named FILEPATH against the exact-implementation ledger on PATH, with no date or record linkage, so a target absorbed by a July run makes today's run for the same file report absorbed. agent-artifact-continuity proves a run was normalized. Neither opens the rendered page and checks the text the recommendation said had to be there.

It graded bookkeeping, process or new-page style, and turned main red on content motion.

validators.title: Favicon, og:image, homepage JSON-LD, AEO definition + speakable, Clarity and IndexNow key stay in place
validators.risk_prevented: Measured 10 Oct 2026 on theindustryguides.com: /favicon.ico 404, no og:image on any page, no FAQPage or BreadcrumbList on the homepage and no definition paragraph for answer engines. Each item is registered in data/seo/site_hygiene_registry.json; this fails if a rebuild, content cycle or refactor drops any of them (files, build-chain step, homepage schema/definition/speakable, Clarity id, IndexNow key file).
validators.why_existing_checks_do_not_cover: homepage-schema is a warning that asserts entity nodes only; nothing checked favicon, og:image, the definition paragraph, speakable selectors, the Clarity map or the IndexNow key file.
validators.unit_attribution_measured: Each array was produced against a constructed failing state on 2026-10-11 (see the PR): removing favicon.ico, swapping og.png for a 1x1 PNG, renaming FAQPage on the homepage, moving the definition below another element, changing the Clarity id, deleting the IndexNow key file, and dropping install_site_head_assets.js from npm run build.
validators.failure_action: Fix at the source: data/seo/site_brand_assets.json + root brand files, scripts/install_site_head_assets.js, the homepage builder in scripts/build_site.js (HOME_DEFINITION / HOME_FAQ), data/clarity_projects.json. Never edit rendered pages.

lineage_policy.authority: _validation_registry.json is the executable source of truth for validation selection, dependency order, prerequisites, outputs, severity, and mutation boundaries.
lineage_policy.dependency_rule: Dependencies are included recursively and executed in topological order before dependents.
lineage_policy.prerequisite_rule: Missing required files trigger registered prepare_commands. Unregistered preparation is forbidden.
lineage_policy.mutation_rule: Validator commands may write only declared mutates_files. Source roots are hash-checked before and after each validator.
lineage_policy.output_rule: Declared produces_files must exist after a passing validator.

release_blocking_policy.clarification: Whitespace inside a URL or href remains a broken-link defect, not a formatting defect.

self_heal_policy.note: A validator may declare repair_command when a repair exists that targets the same defect it detects. The loop runs the profile, repairs what failed, and re-validates, up to --max attempts. Validators without a repair are reported by name rather than retried, because another identical pass would not change the result.
self_heal_policy.never: Do not pair a validator with a repair that merely makes it stop failing. A repair that hides a defect is worse than a red build.
